title: FDA Expectations for INDs Combining Two Investigational Oncology Agents: Contribution of Components and Dose Finding
summary: What FDA expects in INDs pairing two investigational cancer drugs: codevelopment criteria, contribution-of-components evidence, nonclinical support, and combination dose-finding designs.
body_markdown:
## FDA expectations for INDs combining two investigational oncology agents: contribution of components and dose finding


When a sponsor wants to take two unapproved agents into the clinic together for cancer, FDA's expectations come from several overlapping documents rather than one guidance. The foundation is the final guidance *Codevelopment of Two or More New Investigational Drugs for Use in Combination* . Sitting on top of it are:


- the 2025 draft *Development of Cancer Drugs for Use in Novel Combination – Determining the Contribution of the Individual Drugs' Effects*
- the final oncology dosage optimization guidance
- the 2022 expansion cohort guidance
- ICH S9 and its Q&A, for nonclinical support[124](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=124)[135](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=135)[80](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=80)[21](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=21)[65](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=65) .


This article summarizes what those documents ask a sponsor to show at the IND stage and in early-phase design.


### 1. Is codevelopment justified? The threshold criteria


The codevelopment guidance covers two or more drugs that have not been developed for any indication and are intended to be used together. It does not cover combinations of approved drugs, or a new drug combined with an approved drug[124](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=124)[125](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=125) . FDA states plainly that codeveloping drugs generally produces less information about each drug's safety, effectiveness, and dose-response than developing them separately[126](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=126) .


For that reason, FDA says codevelopment should *ordinarily* be reserved for programs that meet **all** of the following criteria[265](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=265) :


Criterion What FDA expects


Serious disease The combination is intended to treat a serious disease or condition[265](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=265)


Strong biological rationale The disease or tumor biology makes the combination plausible. One example is targeting different steps in a cell-proliferation pathway, or reducing resistance[127](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=127)[265](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=265)


Evidence of advance Nonclinical or short-term biomarker evidence suggests a significant advance over available therapy and superiority to the individual agents[265](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=265)[97](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=97)


Compelling reason not to develop separately For example, monotherapy rapidly produces resistance or has very limited activity[265](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=265)


FDA recommends consulting the agency before starting clinical development[265](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=265) . For cancer combinations specifically, the 2025 draft says a novel combination should be considered for development when the necessity of each drug is supported by a strong biologic rationale, including nonclinical characterization of each drug and early clinical evidence. Relevant evidence includes nonclinical or short-term biomarker findings that a drug with limited expected monotherapy activity potentiates its partner[46](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=46) .


### 2. Nonclinical package to support the combination IND


#### Biological rationale and contribution in models


Sponsors should support the rationale in a relevant model. An in vivo model is preferred, but an in vitro model is acceptable. The model should compare the combination with each individual drug and show substantial combination activity. It should also show greater activity, a more durable response, and/or a better toxicity profile than either drug alone[128](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=128)[67](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=67) . Such models may also inform the relative doses of the two agents[67](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=67) .


#### Toxicology: oncology differs from the general M3(R2) default


Outside oncology, ICH M3(R2) recommends a nonclinical combination toxicity study to support clinical trials of two early-stage entities. When it is warranted, the study generally uses one relevant species, and its duration matches the clinical trial up to 90 days[64](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=64) .


For drugs intended to treat patients with advanced cancer, ICH S9 takes a different position:


- Each drug should first be well studied individually in toxicology, and the combination rationale should be provided before the clinical study[65](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=65) .
- Dedicated combination toxicology studies are **generally not warranted** for advanced-cancer combinations, particularly when human toxicity profiles are already characterized[65](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=65) .
- If at least one agent's human toxicity profile is not characterized, provide a combination pharmacology study. It should show increased activity without a substantial increase in toxicity on limited endpoints such as mortality, clinical signs, and body weight. The available information then determines whether dedicated combination toxicology is warranted[65](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=65) .


The S9 Q&A adds several clarifications[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=66)[90](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=90)[91](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=91)[92](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=92) :


- "Well studied individually" means toxicology sufficient to support clinical study of each drug alone[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=66)[90](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=90) .
- When human safety data for a component are absent or very limited, consider a combination pharmacology study **in addition to** single-agent toxicology[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=66)[90](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=90) .
- For drugs that are inactive in animal species, relevant in vitro tests or an understanding of target biology can support the assessment[90](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=90) .
- The rationale should, where feasible, include evidence of increased antitumor activity from pharmacology studies or the literature[91](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=91) .
- If the available clinical and nonclinical data cannot establish a safe starting dose for the combination, a dedicated combination toxicology study may be needed[92](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=92) .


When human safety data for the individual drugs are limited, the codevelopment guidance likewise notes that additional nonclinical data may be needed before human combination studies. In that case the nonclinical combination studies should support initial human dosing and include PK/ADME, toxicokinetic, and relevant biomarker or target-interaction data[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=68)[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=69) .


### 3. IND structure for two investigational agents


The codevelopment guidance ties IND structure to the sponsor's development intent[188](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=188) :


- **Committed to codevelopment:** By the time combination clinical studies begin, one IND should cover all drugs in the combination[189](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=189) .
- **Undecided:** Preliminary proof-of-concept combination studies may run under one drug's IND, provided an individual-drug IND is in effect for each drug. If the sponsor then pursues the combination, it can use that IND as the combination IND or submit a new one[190](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=190) .
- **Also developing either drug as monotherapy:** File a separate IND for the combination and for each individually developed drug[191](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=191) .


The combination IND may cross-reference the individual-drug INDs. If an individual-drug IND belongs to another sponsor, written authorization to cross-reference is required[192](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=192) . Where separate INDs exist, each must have its own annual report, and the reports should cross-reference one another[194](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=194) . FDA encourages contact with the review division as early as possible, for example at a pre-IND meeting. Phase 3 design should be discussed at an end-of-phase-2 meeting[195](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=195)[196](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=196) .


### 4. Phase 1: sequencing and dose finding for the combination


#### Characterize each agent first where possible


FDA's approach depends on the case. It does not require both drugs to complete development alone before they are combined. Still, whenever possible, each drug's safety should first be characterized in phase 1 as it would be for a single agent: maximum tolerated dose, dose-limiting toxicity, and pharmacokinetics. If even short-term monotherapy is unethical or infeasible, nonclinical combination data should support initial human dosing[156](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=156) . Early human studies should characterize safety and PK for both the individual drugs and the combination, so that phase 2 dosing is supported[267](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=267) .


#### Setting the combination starting dose and escalation


- Use the individual drugs' phase 1 safety data, when available, as the primary basis for the combination's starting dose, escalation intervals, and dose-response doses. If those data are not available, nonclinical combination data may be needed[157](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=157) .
- If feasible, evaluate each drug's dose-response to pick the doses to explore in combination. If the drugs cannot be given alone, assess different doses of each **in combination**[158](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=158)[264](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=264) .
- The safety assessment should account for prior human experience and for possible PK, PD, and toxicologic interactions, including shared target-organ toxicity and narrow safety margins[268](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=268) .


#### Clinical pharmacology expectations


Each drug should be studied much as if it were being developed separately. That includes PK, bioavailability, mass balance, the effects of organ impairment, food, and drug interactions, and exposure-response. In vitro metabolism and transporter data should guide whether in vivo drug-drug interaction studies are needed[264](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=264) . If an interaction is found and its mechanism (PK, PD, or overlapping toxicity) is unclear, FDA urges studies to understand it[287](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=287)[288](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=288) .


#### Dosage optimization: moving beyond the MTD


FDA's final oncology dosage optimization guidance cautions that the MTD paradigm was developed for cytotoxic chemotherapy. For many targeted agents, a lower dose may give similar activity with fewer toxicities[80](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=80) . Its recommendations carry over directly to a combination program:


- Compare **multiple dosages** in trials designed to assess activity, safety, and tolerability. A randomized, parallel dose-response design is preferred[81](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=81) .
- Select dosages using more than DLTs. Relevant data include PD, low-grade symptomatic toxicities, dose modifications, tolerability, activity, and preliminary dose- and exposure-response relationships[219](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=219) .
- Include a PK sampling plan in every protocol. In dose-finding trials, it should characterize PK after the first dose and at steady state at each dosage evaluated[218](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=218) .
- When expansion cohorts compare dosages or schedules, randomize to two or more regimens and justify a sample size able to detect clinically important differences[222](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=222) .
- For a new combination, consider existing dose- and exposure-response data. If the data do not support the proposed dosages, conduct additional dose finding, where quantitative modeling may help[285](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=285) .
- Discuss dosage optimization plans with FDA at formal meetings, including early in clinical development[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=223) . Plan to identify an optimized dosage before the marketing application[224](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=224) .


FDA's master-protocol guidance gives a concrete expectation for novel-combination substudies. Identify an RP2D for each individual drug when each may have antitumor activity. Dose finding is appropriate if the combination's RP2D is not established. Before efficacy evaluation, safety data should be available from at least six subjects treated at the proposed combination dosage, and the dose-finding results should be submitted to the IND[290](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=290) . That guidance also asks for a summary of safety, pharmacology, and preliminary efficacy for each investigational drug, plus the combination rationale and any evidence of synergy[291](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=291) .


The 2025 contribution-of-effect draft does **not** address safety or dosing considerations for combination trials. It defers those topics to the codevelopment guidance[240](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=240)[289](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=289) .


### 5. Expansion cohorts that test the combination


Under the 2022 expansion cohort guidance, a cohort testing an investigational drug with another investigational or approved drug should begin only after each investigational drug's preliminary single-agent safety profile has been characterized at its recommended phase 2 dose. The protocol should justify the combination scientifically and include a monitoring plan for overlapping or potentially synergistic toxicities[21](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=21) .


The same guidance sets out IND-level expectations for first-in-human multiple expansion cohort trials:


- **Cohort content:** a scientific rationale, endpoints, eligibility, monitoring plan, and statistical justification of sample size for each cohort. Type I error should be addressed where cohorts are compared[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=22) .
- **Safety reporting:** cumulative safety submissions more frequent than annually, at an interval agreed with FDA[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=22)[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=28) .
- **Cover letter:** the original IND cover letter should clearly identify the trial as a first-in-human multiple expansion cohort trial[23](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=23) .
- **Independent oversight:** an IDMC or another independent entity for all such protocols. Its role includes real-time review of serious adverse events and assessment of each cohort's safety and futility[26](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=26)[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=27) .


### 6. Demonstrating contribution of each component


#### Codevelopment guidance: phase 2 design scenarios


Phase 2 should establish each drug's contribution where needed and possible, show that the combination is effective, and optimize dosing for phase 3. A factorial design is generally preferred[159](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=159)[98](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=98) . The recommended design depends on how much each drug can do alone:


Scenario Recommended design


Both drugs active and can be given separately Four-arm comparison: AB vs A vs B vs placebo or SOC. An adaptive variant can stop poorly performing monotherapy arms early[98](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=98)[160](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=160)[99](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=99)


One drug minimally active alone That drug generally need not be studied alone beyond initial phase 1 safety work. A three-arm A vs AB vs SOC design can show contribution[161](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=161)


Neither drug can be given separately for an effectiveness assessment Compare AB with SOC (or an SOC add-on design) for proof of concept[161](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=161)[266](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=266)


#### 2025 oncology draft on contribution of effect


The July 2025 draft defines "contribution of effect" as showing that each drug contributes to the overall treatment effect observed in the population[135](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=135)[136](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=136) . It applies to the following[137](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=137)[138](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=138) :


- combinations of two or more investigational drugs
- an investigational drug combined with a drug approved for another indication
- drugs approved for different indications


It excludes add-on trials against a drug approved for the same indication[137](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=137)[138](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=138) . Key positions:


- **A randomized factorial trial is highly recommended when feasible.** The traditional design includes the combination arm, each monotherapy arm, and SOC if SOC is not one of the monotherapies[109](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=109)[139](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=139) .
- **Randomized evidence is preferred.** Earlier randomized trials using response rate or another direct measure of anticancer effect are preferred over comparisons with external data[140](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=140)[108](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=108) .
- **Alternatives to full factorial designs** may be appropriate when monotherapy activity is limited, or when preliminary data suggest a large combination effect on a well-characterized outcome. The trials used to isolate contribution must still be adequate and well controlled[129](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=129) .
- **External data** have defined limits. Complete, high-quality patient-level data from a contemporaneous or earlier trial may supplement or replace single-agent arms. Published summary-level results generally serve only to generate hypotheses[131](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=131) . Plans to use external data should be discussed with FDA in advance[131](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=131)[144](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=144) .
- **Nonclinical evidence helps but has limits.** It can reduce uncertainty, but clinical information is generally more compelling because preclinical models do not necessarily predict clinical activity[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=133)[143](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=143) .


The draft is nonbinding and not for implementation. It was issued as a draft in July 2025, so check whether a final version has since been published. It encourages consultation with the review division as early as possible, for example at a pre-IND meeting, and frequently during complex programs[135](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=135)[109](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=109) .


### Practical IND checklist


Drawing the documents together, an IND for an early-phase oncology trial combining two investigational agents should be ready to address the following:


1. **Justification:** where neither drug has been developed for any indication (the codevelopment guidance's scope), why the codevelopment criteria are met, including serious disease, biological rationale, evidence of advance, and why the agents cannot be developed separately[265](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=265) .
2. **Nonclinical package:** single-agent toxicology for each drug, plus a combination pharmacology study or combination toxicology where human data for a component are lacking or a safe combination starting dose cannot otherwise be set[65](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=65)[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=66)[92](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=92) .
3. **IND structure:** a single combination IND or separate INDs, with cross-reference authorizations in place[189](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=189)[191](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=191)[192](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=192) .
4. **Phase 1 design:** single-agent characterization where feasible. The combination starting dose and escalation should rest on individual-drug data, with interaction-focused safety monitoring[156](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=156)[157](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=157)[268](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=268) .
5. **Dosage optimization:** comparison of more than one dosage, PK at each dose level, and early discussion of the strategy with FDA[81](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=81)[218](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=218)[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=223) .
6. **Expansion cohorts:** combination cohorts only after single-agent RP2D safety is established. For first-in-human multiple expansion cohort trials, add independent safety oversight and an agreed cumulative safety reporting cadence[21](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=21)[26](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=26)[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=28) .
7. **Contribution-of-effect plan:** a prospective strategy using a factorial design or a justified alternative, aligned with FDA before external data are relied on[98](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=98)[109](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=109)[131](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expectations-for-inds-combining-two?showSourceNumber=131) .


Questions worth taking further with Rhizome include how specific CDER oncology review divisions have applied these principles in recent approvals, and how the 2025 draft's contribution standards compare with EMA's approach to fixed and free combinations.
